messages.subject: stat_smooth question
parts:
Hi:
I wonder why 'gam' (mymodel below) produces different values than the
values
used by stat_smooth to plot the confidence band. I am using the same
formula
for both but for some reason the gray shaded area is wider than the
dotted lines.
Could someone run the code below and let me know if I am missing
something?

library(mgcv)
library(ggplot2)
# Fit the model
data(cars)
mymodel <- gam(dist ~ s(speed,bs = "cs"), data = cars);mymodel
summary(mymodel)
# Predict dist with GAM and plot using stat_smooth
predd <- cbind(cars,predict(mymodel,cars,se.fit=T));predd
gam_fit <- ggplot(aes(x = speed, y = dist), data = predd) +
geom_point() +
stat_smooth(size=2,colour='red',alpha=0.2,method=gam, formula =
formula <- y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"))
gam_fit
# Add the fitted values and the confidence bands using fit-se.fit
and fit+se.fit
gam_fit + geom_line(aes(y=fit),colour='green') +
geom_line(aes(y=fit-se.fit),linetype=2,colour='blue',size=1) +
geom_line(aes(y=fit+se.fit),linetype=2,colour='blue',size=1)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: stat_smooth question
parts:
Hi Felipe:

The se.fit = TRUE option in predict.gam() from mgcv returns the
standard error, so fit +/- SE is an approximate 68% confidence band
(using the normal as a reference distribution). By default, the
confidence bands returned by geom_smooth() have default level 95%. If
you take the following code and add level = 0.68 to the argument list
of stat_smooth(), you'll see that the shading matches the 1 SE curves
around the fit.

Dennis

gam_fit2 <- ggplot(aes(x = speed, y = dist), data = predd) +
geom_point() +
stat_smooth(size=1.5, colour='red', method="gam", level = 0.68,
formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs")) +
